content.text:
There's an `entire doctor` command for exactly this. Since the sandbox where this happened isn't this session's working directory, run it there:

```bash
entire doctor
```

**What the error means:** the stop hook tried to write a checkpoint and Entire's local object store hit a rename race — `objects/pack/tmp_obj_...` no longer existed when it tried to move it into its final content-addressed path (`objects/45/853a99...`). That's the object-store equivalent of git's `renameat` failure: either a concurrent Entire process in the same `.entire` directory already consumed/cleaned that temp file, or something (AV, sync client) touched it mid-write. It says **non-blocking**, so your actual work/commit is unaffected — only that one checkpoint step failed to save.

Fix path:
1. Run `entire doctor` in that sandbox — it's built for diagnosing/repairing exactly this kind of session-data corruption.
2. If it recurs repeatedly (not just once), check whether two agent processes/sandboxes are writing checkpoints into the *same* `.entire` object store concurrently — that's the known race, not a one-off disk hiccup.

Want me to look deeper, or is `entire doctor` enough to try first?

Scan for session issues and offer to fix them.

Checks performed:
  1. Disconnected metadata branches: detects when local and remote
     entire/checkpoints/v1 branches share no common ancestor (caused by a
     previous bug). Fixes by cherry-picking local checkpoints onto remote tip.

  When Codex hooks are installed:
  2. Codex hook trust: warn when hooks declared in .codex/hooks.json
     lack a trusted_hash entry in the user's Codex config (i.e. /hooks
     review hasn't run yet on this machine, or a newer entire release
     added a hook the user hasn't approved yet).

  For each installed agent that reports hook-config drift:
  3. Hook config: warn when the installed hooks no longer match what this
     CLI writes (e.g. an older release wrote Claude Code tool matchers that
     no longer fire, or a committed Pi/OpenCode extension has gone stale).
     Fix by re-running 'entire enable --force'.

  4. Stuck sessions: sessions stuck in ACTIVE or ENDED phase that need cleanup.

A session is considered stuck if:
  - It is in ACTIVE phase with no interaction for over 1 hour
  - It is in ENDED phase with uncondensed checkpoint data on a shadow branch

For each stuck session, you can choose to:
  - Condense: Save session data to permanent storage
  - Discard: Remove the session state and shadow branch data
  - Skip: Leave the session as-is

Use --force to condense all fixable sessions without prompting.  Sessions that can't
be condensed will be discarded.

file.content:
---
name: powerline-statusline-reaches-sandboxes-by-kit
description: The claude-powerline statusline reaches sbx sandboxes through a kit at ~/projects/sbx-kits/claude-powerline, loaded by the `claude` shell function.
metadata:
  type: project
---

The statusline is **not** the plugin: `~/.claude/settings.json` sets
`statusLine.command`, and the `claude-powerline@claude-powerline` plugin only adds the
`/powerline` skill. Reproducing it in a sandbox needs three things — the binary, the
`~/.claude/claude-powerline.json` config, and the `statusLine` key.

Kit: `C:\Users\anthoni\projects\sbx-kits\claude-powerline` (mixin, `requires.agent: claude`).
It `npm install -g`s the package rather than keeping the host's
`npx -y @owloops/claude-powerline@latest` — that command runs on *every* statusline render.
A startup script **merges** the `statusLine` key with node; writing a whole
`settings.json` through `setup.files` would erase the sandbox's own
`defaultMode: bypassPermissions`.

Two mechanics worth remembering:

- `sbx kit add` refuses any kit declaring `setup.startup` ("the kit-add recreate flow does
  not yet apply" it). Adding such a kit to an existing sandbox means `sbx rm` + `sbx create --kit`.
- `--kit` applies at **creation** only; re-attaching ignores it, like `--publish`.
- Kit file `content:` rejects `${...}` other than `${WORKDIR}` — plain JS template literals
  fail validation.

Loaded by `function claude { sbx run --kit "$env:SBX_KITS\claude-powerline" claude @args }`
in the PowerShell profile. Related: [[sbx-shares-only-flat-claude-skills]]

schemaVersion: "2"
kind: mixin
name: entire-push
version: "1.0.0"
displayName: entire git push
description: >
  Installs the entire and git-remote-entire binaries so a sandbox can push
  through the entire:// mirror itself, instead of handing push/PR commands
  back to the host. Requires a ENTIRE_TOKEN secret wired on the host with
  `sbx secret set-custom` (see README.md next to this file) — the binaries
  alone are not enough, git-remote-entire still needs a bearer token to
  authenticate against the mirror.

requires:
  agent: claude

permissions:
  network:
    allow:
      - github.com
      - objects.githubusercontent.com
      - aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
      - us.auth.entire.io
      - docs.entire.io
      - example.com

setup:
  install:
    - command: |
        set -e
        case "$(uname -m)" in
          x86_64|amd64) ARCH=amd64 ;;
          aarch64|arm64) ARCH=arm64 ;;
          *) echo "unsupported arch: $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
        esac
        VERSION=0.10.2
        curl -fsSL "https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/download/v${VERSION}/entire_linux_${ARCH}.tar.gz" \
          | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin entire git-remote-entire
        chmod +x /usr/local/bin/entire /usr/local/bin/git-remote-entire
      user: "0"
      description: Install entire and git-remote-entire binaries from the GitHub release

content.text:
`entire` in the sandbox is installed by the `entire-push` kit (`~/projects/sbx-kits/entire-push/spec.yaml`), pinned to `VERSION=0.10.2` at line 36 — it's baked in at `setup.install`, not something ambient in the base image.

Two consequences, given the `--kit` mechanics from the powerline kit:

- **Just running the update command inside the running sandbox** (`curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`) works *for that sandbox's current lifetime only*. Nothing persists it — the next time this sandbox is recreated (or a fresh one is spun up with `--kit entire-push`), it reinstalls 0.10.2 from the pinned version in the kit and you're back to the old binary.
- **To make the update stick**, edit the kit itself: bump `VERSION: 0.10.2` → `0.10.3` in `spec.yaml`. That only takes effect for sandboxes created *after* the edit — `--kit` applies at creation only, so an existing sandbox won't pick it up just by re-attaching (same caveat as the powerline kit).

So: if you just want this one sandbox fixed right now, run the curl command inside it. If you want every future sandbox to get 0.10.3, edit the kit's version pin and recreate.

Want me to bump the version in `spec.yaml`?

content.content:
Run an agent in a sandbox, creating the sandbox if it does not already exist.

The first positional argument is the agent to run. To re-attach to an existing
sandbox by name, use --name; the agent positional is optional when the named
sandbox already exists and is read from its spec.

Pass agent arguments after the "--" separator. Additional workspaces can be
provided as extra arguments. Append ":ro" to mount them read-only.

To create a sandbox without attaching, use "sbx create" instead, or
pass --detached (-d) to print the sandbox ID and exit without opening an
interactive session.

Available agents: claude, codex, copilot, cursor, docker-agent, droid, gemini, kiro, opencode, shell

Usage:
  sbx run [flags] [AGENT] [PATH...] [-- AGENT_ARGS...]

Examples:
  # Create and run a sandbox with claude in current directory
  sbx run claude

  # Create and run with additional workspaces (read-only)
  sbx run claude . /path/to/docs:ro

  # Re-attach to an existing sandbox by name (agent read from its spec)
  sbx run --name existing-sandbox

  # Re-attach to an existing sandbox by name and verify the expected agent
  sbx run claude --name existing-sandbox

  # Run a sandbox with agent arguments
  sbx run claude -- --continue

Flags:
      --clone                               Run the agent on a private in-container clone of the host Git repository; must be set at sandbox creation time (no-op when re-attaching to an existing clone-mode sandbox)
      --cpus int                            Number of CPUs to allocate to the sandbox (0 = auto: all host CPUs)
      --deny-network sbx policy ls <NAME>   Add a per-sandbox network deny rule at creation time. Can be specified multiple times. The rule applies only to the new sandbox and can be listed or removed later with sbx policy ls <NAME> / `sbx policy rm network --sandbox <NAME> --resource <HOST>`. Safe under centralized governance because a local deny can only narrow, never widen, egress.
  -e, --env stringArray                     Set an environment variable in the sandbox (can be repeated): KEY=VALUE, or a bare KEY to take the value from the current environment. Applies to the agent session, so it takes effect on a re-attach too; also baked into the sandbox when this run creates it
      --env-file stringArray                Read environment variables from a file (can be repeated). --env wins over any file; a later file wins over an earlier one. Applies to the agent session, so it takes effect on a re-attach too; also baked into the sandbox when this run creates it
  -h, --help                                help for run
      --kit strings                         (Experimental) Kit reference (directory, ZIP, or OCI). Can be specified multiple times
  -m, --memory string                       Memory limit in binary units (e.g., 1024m, 8g). Default: 50% of host memory, max 32 GiB
      --name string                         Name for the sandbox (default: <agent>-<workdir>)
      --profile string                      Governance profile to assign to the sandbox
  -p, --publish stringArray                 Publish a sandbox port to the host (can be repeated): [[HOST_IP:]HOST_PORT:]SANDBOX_PORT[/PROTOCOL]. Applied when the sandbox is created; ignored when re-attaching (use "sbx ports")
      --static-mcp strings                  MCP server names that form the sandbox's fixed (static) MCP set. Accepts a comma-separated list (--static-mcp notion,atlassian), repeated flags (--static-mcp notion --static-mcp atlassian), or a mix; all forms accumulate into the same set. The set is chosen once at creation time and cannot be changed when re-attaching to an existing sandbox.
  -t, --template string                     Container image to use for the sandbox (default: agent-specific image)

Global Flags:
  -D, --debug   Enable debug logging

content.text:
Different mechanism than `entire` — there's no kit pinning Claude Code's version. It comes from two places:

1. **The base image.** `sbx template ls` shows the sandbox is created from `docker.io/docker/sandbox-templates:claude-code-docker` (Docker's official image, pulled fresh ~1h ago) — that's where the `claude` binary is baked in, not something wired through your `~/projects/sbx-kits/*`. Whatever version ships in that image is what a brand-new sandbox starts with.

2. **Claude Code's own auto-updater.** Unlike `entire`, the CLI self-updates on launch by default (same as on the host) — so in practice you usually don't manage it, it keeps itself current unless auto-update is disabled with `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`.

So the two levers:
- **Just let it be** — default behavior, self-updates each run.
- **Pin it** — set `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` via `sbx run --env DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 claude ...` (or bake it in a kit's `setup.install`/env) if you want a sandbox frozen at whatever the image shipped.

One thing worth flagging: `sbx template ls` also shows a stale local snapshot, `localhost:5000/sandbox-mise:claude-code`, saved 3 months ago via `sbx template save`. If anything (a script, a habit) launches sandboxes with `-t sandbox-mise:claude-code` instead of the default, it's running a 3-month-old Claude Code frozen at whatever that snapshot had — worth checking you're not accidentally pinned there.

file.content:
# entire-push kit

Installs `entire` and `git-remote-entire` in the sandbox so a session can
push through the `entire://` mirror itself, instead of handing push/PR
commands back to the host (as happened on `fix/datatable-empty-body-rule139`).

## One-time host setup

The binaries alone can't authenticate. Wire a token as a custom secret once,
on the host:

```bash
sbx secret set-custom \
  --host aws-eu-central-1.entire.io \
  --host us.auth.entire.io \
  --env ENTIRE_TOKEN \
  --command "entire auth token" \
  --refresh 55m
```

This stores the *command*, not a static token — `sbx` re-runs `entire auth
token` on the host and refreshes the sandbox's placeholder value every 55
minutes (the same cadence `entire auth token` itself uses to refresh a
near-expiry login JWT). The sandbox only ever sees a placeholder in
`ENTIRE_TOKEN`; the proxy substitutes the real bearer token on outbound
requests to the two hosts above.

If push still fails from other `*.entire.io` subdomains (a different
jurisdiction cell, for example), add more `--host` entries to the same
secret with `sbx secret set-custom ... --host <new-host>` — `set-custom`
overwrites in place when given the same `--env`/scope.

## Usage

```powershell
sbx run --kit "$env:SBX_KITS\entire-push" claude .
```

`--kit` only applies at sandbox **creation** (like `--publish`); re-attaching
to an existing sandbox ignores it. Adding it to an already-created sandbox
needs `sbx rm` + `sbx create --kit` — `sbx kit add` refuses kits that
declare `setup.startup`, but this one only declares `setup.install`, so
`sbx kit add` should work here too if you want to retrofit a running
sandbox.

## Why this instead of the host relaying pushes

Direct-mode sandboxes mount the host repo, so commits already land on the
host with no push needed — that part of the flow was already correct. This
kit is for closing the gap where a sandbox session wants to also push and
open the PR itself, without a human relaying `git push` / `gh pr create`
from the host each time.

content.content:
Install a plugin.

Three source forms:

  name   Bare names resolve through the plugin index:
             entire plugin install run
  url    Full git repository URLs install from any git host. The newest
         semver tag is resolved with 'git ls-remote'; the platform's release
         asset is downloaded over HTTPS and verified against the release's
         checksums.txt. A release that publishes no checksums is refused
         unless --allow-unverified is passed:
             entire plugin install https://github.com/entireio/entire-run
  path   Local executables are linked into the managed directory (symlink
         first, so rebuilds are picked up immediately). Paths must be
         explicit — a separator or leading ./ — so a stray local file can
         never shadow an index name:
             entire plugin install ./dist/entire-run
             entire plugin install ./entire-run

Installing from a URL that is not listed in the plugin index asks for
confirmation; pass --yes to skip (required in non-interactive runs).

Plugins may declare dependencies in entire-plugin.yml. Missing dependencies
are listed and installed after a single confirmation (or with --yes);
--no-deps opts out.

Usage:
  entire plugin install <name|url|path> [flags]

Flags:
      --allow-unverified   Install even when the release publishes no checksums.txt to authenticate the download
      --force              Replace an existing entry with the same name
  -h, --help               help for install
      --index string       Plugin index URL (overrides ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL and the built-in default)
      --no-deps            Do not install declared dependencies
      --pin string         Install exactly this tag and skip it during 'plugin upgrade'
      --yes                Skip confirmation prompts (non-index sources, dependency installs)

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

1	schemaVersion: "2"
2	kind: mixin
3	name: claude-powerline
4	version: "1.0.0"
5	displayName: claude-powerline statusline
6	description: Installs @owloops/claude-powerline and wires it into the sandbox statusLine.
7	
8	requires:
9	  agent: claude
10	
11	permissions:
12	  network:
13	    allow:
14	      - registry.npmjs.org
15	
16	setup:
17	  install:
18	    - command: npm install -g @owloops/claude-powerline@latest
19	      user: "0"
20	      description: Install the claude-powerline binary globally
21	
22	    # Belt-and-braces alongside setup.startup below: docker/sbx-releases#189 —
23	    # a kit's setup.startup can silently fail to fire when stacked with other
24	    # --kit flags, with no error output. setup.install is the phase that's
25	    # actually reliable when kits are combined, so the merge happens here too
26	    # (inline, since setup.install runs before setup.files exists yet).
27	    - command: |
28	        node <<'EOF'
29	        const { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync } = require("node:fs");
30	        const { dirname, join } = require("node:path");
31	        const p = join(process.env.HOME, ".claude", "settings.json");
32	        let s = {};
33	        try { s = JSON.parse(readFileSync(p, "utf8")); } catch {}
34	        s.statusLine = { type: "command", command: "claude-powerline" };
35	        mkdirSync(dirname(p), { recursive: true });
36	        writeFileSync(p, JSON.stringify(s, null, 2) + "\n");
37	        console.log("statusLine ->", s.statusLine.command);
38	        EOF
39	      user: "1000"
40	      description: Merge statusLine at install time, in case setup.startup never fires
41	
42	  files:
43	    - path: /home/agent/.local/bin/wire-powerline.mjs
44	      mode: "0755"
45	      description: Merge statusLine into the agent settings without clobbering them
46	      content: |
47	        import { readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
48	        import { dirname, join } from "node:path";
49	        const p = join(process.env.HOME, ".claude", "settings.json");
50	        let s = {};
51	        try { s = JSON.parse(readFileSync(p, "utf8")); } catch {}
52	        s.statusLine = { type: "command", command: "claude-powerline" };
53	        mkdirSync(dirname(p), { recursive: true });
54	        writeFileSync(p, JSON.stringify(s, null, 2) + "\n");
55	        console.log("statusLine ->", s.statusLine.command);
56	
57	  startup:
58	    - command: ["node", "/home/agent/.local/bin/wire-powerline.mjs"]

name: entire-push
version: "1.0.0"
displayName: entire git push
description: >
  Installs the entire and git-remote-entire binaries so a sandbox can push
  through the entire:// mirror itself, instead of handing push/PR commands
  back to the host. Requires a ENTIRE_TOKEN secret wired on the host with
  `sbx secret set-custom` (see README.md next to this file) — the binaries
  alone are not enough, git-remote-entire still needs a bearer token to
  authenticate against the mirror.

requires:
  agent: claude

permissions:
  network:
    allow:
      - github.com
      - objects.githubusercontent.com
      - aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
      - us.auth.entire.io
      - docs.entire.io
      - example.com

setup:
  install:
    - command: |
        set -e
        case "$(uname -m)" in
          x86_64|amd64) ARCH=amd64 ;;
          aarch64|arm64) ARCH=arm64 ;;
          *) echo "unsupported arch: $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
        esac
        VERSION=0.10.2
        curl -fsSL "https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/download/v${VERSION}/entire_linux_${ARCH}.tar.gz" \
          | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin entire git-remote-entire
        chmod +x /usr/local/bin/entire /usr/local/bin/git-remote-entire
      user: "0"
      description: Install entire and git-remote-entire binaries from the GitHub release

file.content:
# entire-push kit

Installs `entire` and `git-remote-entire` in the sandbox so a session can
push through the `entire://` mirror itself, instead of handing push/PR
commands back to the host (as happened on `fix/datatable-empty-body-rule139`).

## One-time host setup

The binaries alone can't authenticate. Wire a token as a custom secret once,
on the host:

```bash
sbx secret set-custom \
  --host aws-eu-central-1.entire.io \
  --host us.auth.entire.io \
  --env ENTIRE_TOKEN \
  --command "entire auth token" \
  --refresh 55m
```

This stores the *command*, not a static token — `sbx` re-runs `entire auth
token` on the host and refreshes the sandbox's placeholder value every 55
minutes (the same cadence `entire auth token` itself uses to refresh a
near-expiry login JWT). The sandbox only ever sees a placeholder in
`ENTIRE_TOKEN`; the proxy substitutes the real bearer token on outbound
requests to the two hosts above.

If push still fails from other `*.entire.io` subdomains (a different
jurisdiction cell, for example), add more `--host` entries to the same
secret with `sbx secret set-custom ... --host <new-host>` — `set-custom`
overwrites in place when given the same `--env`/scope.

## Usage

```powershell
sbx run --kit "$env:SBX_KITS\entire-push" claude .
```

`--kit` only applies at sandbox **creation** (like `--publish`); re-attaching
to an existing sandbox ignores it. Adding it to an already-created sandbox
needs `sbx rm` + `sbx create --kit` — `sbx kit add` refuses kits that
declare `setup.startup`, but this one only declares `setup.install`, so
`sbx kit add` should work here too if you want to retrofit a running
sandbox.

## Why this instead of the host relaying pushes

Direct-mode sandboxes mount the host repo, so commits already land on the
host with no push needed — that part of the flow was already correct. This
kit is for closing the gap where a sandbox session wants to also push and
open the PR itself, without a human relaying `git push` / `gh pr create`
from the host each time.

file.content:
schemaVersion: "2"
kind: mixin
name: entire
version: "1.0.0"
displayName: entire
description: >
  Installs the entire and git-remote-entire binaries so a sandbox can push
  through the entire:// mirror itself, instead of handing push/PR commands
  back to the host. Requires a ENTIRE_TOKEN secret wired on the host with
  `sbx secret set-custom` (see README.md next to this file) — the binaries
  alone are not enough, git-remote-entire still needs a bearer token to
  authenticate against the mirror. Also installs the `graph` plugin
  (entire-graph) so .entire/graph-agent.md's search-first workflow works
  inside the sandbox instead of silently falling back to grep/find.

requires:
  agent: claude

permissions:
  network:
    allow:
      - github.com
      - objects.githubusercontent.com
      - aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
      - us.auth.entire.io
      - docs.entire.io
      - example.com

setup:
  install:
    - command: |
        set -e
        case "$(uname -m)" in
          x86_64|amd64) ARCH=amd64 ;;
          aarch64|arm64) ARCH=arm64 ;;
          *) echo "unsupported arch: $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
        esac
        VERSION=0.10.2
        curl -fsSL "https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/download/v${VERSION}/entire_linux_${ARCH}.tar.gz" \
          | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin entire git-remote-entire
        chmod +x /usr/local/bin/entire /usr/local/bin/git-remote-entire
      user: "0"
      description: Install entire and git-remote-entire binaries from the GitHub release

    # Runs as the agent user (not root): 'entire plugin install' places the
    # plugin under the CALLING user's managed dir (~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin
    # on Linux), which is only auto-prepended to PATH for that same user at
    # startup. Installing this as root would land it under /root and be
    # invisible to the agent session.
    - command: entire plugin install graph --yes
      user: "1000"
      description: Install the graph plugin (entire-graph) for the agent user

content.content:
title:	v0.10.3
tag:	v0.10.3
draft:	false
prerelease:	false
immutable:	false
author:	github-actions[bot]
created:	2026-08-27T17:15:53Z
published:	2026-08-27T17:28:37Z
url:	https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/tag/v0.10.3
asset:	checksums.txt
asset:	entire_darwin_amd64.tar.gz
asset:	entire_darwin_arm64.tar.gz
asset:	entire_linux_amd64.tar.gz
asset:	entire_linux_arm64.tar.gz
asset:	entire_windows_amd64.zip
asset:	entire_windows_arm64.zip
--

### Added

- Subagent work now survives into committed checkpoints, for every agent that reports subagent completion: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, and Factory AI Droid. 0.10.2 shipped the in-session half and noted that committed checkpoints still carried no per-subagent data for any agent — this is the durable half. A subagent's work becomes a `task_records` ledger on the parent session, and condensation materializes each record's transcript into `tasks/<tool-use-id>/` inside the parent session's checkpoint, so every checkpoint is self-contained; the ledger, the materializer, and the commit linkage are all agent-agnostic. Commits a subagent makes between the parent's turns link to their session too, instead of shipping with no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer at all — six of seven commits on a real subagent-driven branch had gone unlinked. The one agent-specific piece is Claude Code's `SubagentStop` hook, now registered: a backgrounded `Task` fires `PostToolUse` at the launch acknowledgment, before the subagent has done anything, so a session that dispatched 29 background agents running 5–18 minutes each had captured nothing but a launch stub per agent. Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Pi expose no subagent hook and are unchanged ([#2032](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2032), [#2034](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2034))
- An agent's commit links to its session by *who made it*, not by worktree path: the owner fingerprint already recorded at every turn start is matched against the commit hook's own process ancestry, so a commit made in a sibling worktree links automatically with no `entire session adopt`. Nearest ancestor wins for nested agents, host/boot/start-time guards defeat PID reuse, and a human commit typed in the same terminal still never matches. Identity is unioned with worktree matching, never a replacement; on Windows, where the process walk is unavailable, linking is unchanged ([#2013](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2013))
- Zombie sessions self-heal instead of waiting for someone to run `entire doctor`. The session-start hook cheaply detects sessions whose agent died without a stop hook, or that have been sitting on uncondensed checkpoint data for over 24h, and fires a detached `__sweep_sessions` that finalizes and condenses them — one real session had been stuck for 4 days with 60 checkpoints, slowing every commit in the meantime. The hook's own timeout budget is untouched regardless of backlog ([#2029](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2029))
- Teams can choose which secret-scanner engines feed redaction, via `redaction.betterleaks.enabled` and `redaction.goredact.enabled` in committed `.entire/settings.json`. Defaults are unchanged (betterleaks on, goredact off), the keys are deliberately ignored in `settings.local.json` — the choice affects everyone who reads the repo's checkpoints — and disabling both fails settings load rather than shipping unscanned content. If the sole enabled engine fails at runtime, transcript writes fail closed instead of persisting under-scanned data ([#2081](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2081))
- `entire doctor trace --summary` aggregates hook traces into per-hook p50/p90/max with the dominant step, and `--slow` narrows to the slow ones — the question with slow traces accumulating is "what is slow in general", which previously meant hand-rolling a grep over `.entire/logs`. The command's help no longer claims traces need DEBUG to be enabled; they have been emitted at WARN by default since 0.10.1 ([#2092](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2092))
- Redaction diagnostics reach `.entire/logs` and `entire doctor` reports a log directory Entire cannot write to. Pack load failures, rule compile errors and sample mismatches went to the process-default logger — bare stderr, which hook contexts swallow — so a user debugging custom rules could grep for `component=redaction`, find nothing, and reasonably conclude the rules never ran. There is now also one INFO summary per process naming pack/rule/inline counts and PII/OPF state, and an unwritable `.entire/logs` is called out by name instead of presenting as a silent exit 0 ([#1973](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1973), [#2082](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2082))
- `entire trail update --body` sends the description's ETag as `If-Match`, so a body write is rejected rather than silently clobbering a description that changed since it was read. `--overwrite` writes unconditionally, and a server or trail without an etag degrades to the previous behavior ([#2079](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2079))
- Telemetry gained three content-free signals, all gated on the same opt-in setting and `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT`: `cli_skill_invoked` for skill invocations (skill name from a closed vocabulary — no prompt text or arguments), `cli_commit_condensed` for whether a commit landed files already carrying AI checkpoint history without the session ever consulting search, and `cli_search_completed` for whether a search actually returned a usable response rather than just that it ran ([#2023](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2023), [#2024](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2024), [#2100](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2100), [#2130](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2130))

### Changed

- The search TUI scrolls continuously instead of paging 10 results at a time — commit search reads like a pruned `git log`, and the next API page loads automatically as you approach the end. Type tabs move on ←/→ (or tab/shift+tab) with wraparound; the `1`-`3` number keys are gone, and the status row reports `N of M results` instead of `page X/Y` ([#2138](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2138))
- CLI search results match the web's. Per-cell responses were always identical — only the client-side merges diverged: the CLI cut the merged list globally at 100 where the web windows per type, reported summed corpus counts up to 13× larger, deduped every type where the web dedupes sessions only, and dropped every completeness flag. Counts now describe exactly what you can see (with a `+` when lower-bounded), incomplete results are labeled rather than silent, and the retired ANN fallback tail no longer renders ([#2090](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2090))
- A logged-out `git pull` against a cluster now names one login server — `entire login` — instead of printing a list of seven hosts and leaving you to pick, three of which were not login servers at all. Staging still names `--server` where the flag is genuinely required ([#2128](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2128))

### Security

- `task.json`'s `task_description` — the free text an agent writes when dispatching a subagent — was copied verbatim into the pushed checkpoint while the subagent transcript beside it went through the full sanitize → externalize → redact pipeline. The checkpoint writer now redacts it, covering both persistent backends ([#2129](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2129))
- betterleaks moves to 1.8.0, which closes a real under-redaction gap: a bare `password=<secret>` assignment previously escaped every layer. Validated with an A/B diff over 22 real checkpoint transcripts (64MB) — 21 byte-identical, one file with five safe-direction over-redactions of test-fixture passwords, zero under-redactions. The upstream dependency swap also makes the transcript redaction path 1.36× faster and shrinks the binary ([#2042](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2042))

### Fixed

- Every `git status` Entire runs now passes `--no-optional-locks`. `git status` is a write: it refreshes the index's stat cache, holds `.git/index.lock` for the whole worktree walk, and renames a fresh index over `.git/index`. Entire read the porcelain output once and discarded it, so that write bought nothing — but on a filesystem where rename-over-existing is not atomic against a concurrent lookup (virtiofs / gRPC-FUSE bind mounts, i.e. Docker Desktop devcontainers — measured at 9.9% ENOENT across 29,596 opens, versus 0 on ext4) a reader can observe `.git/index` missing, and git treats ENOENT, and only ENOENT, as an *empty* index: a `git commit` landing in that window records the empty tree with exit 0 and no warning. Output is byte-identical with the flag. This removes Entire's contribution rather than the hazard — any concurrent `git status` on an affected mount opens the same window, including several agents working one repo, and the environment-wide mitigation is `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` ([#2143](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2143))
- A Stop hook on a large transcript no longer re-redacts the whole thing. Redaction was 99.7% of the blob write, and because `full.jsonl` is append-only but was re-redacted in full at every checkpoint, a session with N checkpoints re-redacted O(N²) bytes — a 70MB Codex transcript took ~67s. The line pass is now sharded across goroutines (byte-balanced, output byte-identical) and the previous checkpoint's redacted prefix is reused, so only appended lines are redacted: ~66s → **2.0s** on a simulated 14-checkpoint session. Commits a subagent makes between the parent's turns link to their session too, instead of shipping with no `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer at all — six of seven commits on a real subagent-driven branch had gone unlinked. content.text:
Traced this to Entire's own source (`entireio/cli`) — both issues confirmed, and one needs a decision from you.

**1. `ENTIRE_TOKEN` — not a config bug, an architecture mismatch**

`cmd/entire/cli/auth/env_token.go`: `ENTIRE_TOKEN` is documented as the CI/workload-identity path — its value is used **verbatim as the bearer**, and before any network request, `git-remote-entire` calls `tokens.ParseClaims()` on it locally to read the `aud` claim and pick the core URL. It needs the *real* JWT bytes in the process's own env, client-side, before it ever talks to the network.

That's incompatible with how `sbx secret set-custom` works: it hands the sandbox an opaque placeholder (`sbx-cs-...`) and only substitutes the real token *on the wire* for requests to the declared hosts. Local JWT parsing never sees the substitution — it always gets the placeholder, hence `expected 3 segments, got 1`. Host-side everything checks out (`entire auth token` returns a real JWT, `sbx secret list` shows the custom secret correctly wired to both hosts) — there's nothing to fix there. This is a structural limit of combining `ENTIRE_TOKEN` with `sbx secret set-custom`.

Two real options, and this is a security tradeoff only you should make:

| Option | Tradeoff |
|---|---|
| Pass the real JWT directly — `sbx run --kit ... --env ENTIRE_TOKEN=$(entire auth token) claude .` | Sandbox pushes itself, but a real (if short-lived) bearer token sits in plaintext env inside the sandbox instead of never leaving the proxy |
| Drop `ENTIRE_TOKEN` from the sandbox; keep host-relayed push | No token exposure, but back to the original "hand push/PR to host" flow the kit was meant to replace |

Want me to wire one of these into the `entire` kit, or leave it as-is for now?

**2. The renameat race — likely explained, not directly fixed, by 0.10.3**

0.10.3's changelog has a fix for the *exact* filesystem class this sandbox runs on: `git status` now passes `--no-optional-locks` because on **virtiofs / gRPC-FUSE bind mounts (Docker Desktop devcontainers — i.e. what `sbx` uses)** rename-over-existing is non-atomic and measured at **9.9% ENOENT** across 29,596 opens, vs. 0% on ext4. That's the same rename-then-ENOENT shape we're hitting, just against `.entire/objects/pack/tmp_obj_*` (Entire's own blob store) rather than `.git/index` — the fix doesn't explicitly cover that code path, so I can't promise it goes away, but it's the same underlying host-mount hazard. Their own stated environment-wide mitigation is `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.

Also confirmed: nothing in 0.10.3 touches `ENTIRE_TOKEN`/`git-remote-entire` claim parsing — that limitation is still open.

For now, run `entire doctor -f` again in that sandbox to clear the stuck session from this latest checkpoint failure. Say the word if you want me to bump the kit's pinned `VERSION` to 0.10.3 and add `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` to the sandbox env as a mitigation attempt.

file.content:
# entire kit

Installs `entire` and `git-remote-entire` in the sandbox so a session can
push through the `entire://` mirror itself, instead of handing push/PR
commands back to the host.
Also installs the `graph` plugin (`entire-graph`) as the agent user, so
`.entire/graph-agent.md`'s `entire graph search` workflow works inside the
sandbox — without it, a sandbox session has no plugin at
`~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin` and silently falls back to grep/find.

## One-time host setup

The binaries alone can't authenticate. Wire a token as a custom secret once,
on the host:

```bash
sbx secret set-custom \
  --host aws-eu-central-1.entire.io \
  --host us.auth.entire.io \
  --env ENTIRE_TOKEN \
  --command "entire auth token" \
  --refresh 55m
```

This stores the *command*, not a static token — `sbx` re-runs `entire auth
token` on the host and refreshes the sandbox's placeholder value every 55
minutes (the same cadence `entire auth token` itself uses to refresh a
near-expiry login JWT). The sandbox only ever sees a placeholder in
`ENTIRE_TOKEN`; the proxy substitutes the real bearer token on outbound
requests to the two hosts above.

If push still fails from other `*.entire.io` subdomains (a different
jurisdiction cell, for example), add more `--host` entries to the same
secret with `sbx secret set-custom ... --host <new-host>` — `set-custom`
overwrites in place when given the same `--env`/scope.

## Usage

```powershell
sbx run --kit "$env:SBX_KITS\entire" claude .
```

`--kit` only applies at sandbox **creation** (like `--publish`); re-attaching
to an existing sandbox ignores it. Adding it to an already-created sandbox
needs `sbx rm` + `sbx create --kit` — `sbx kit add` refuses kits that
declare `setup.startup`, but this one only declares `setup.install`, so
`sbx kit add` should work here too if you want to retrofit a running
sandbox.

## Why this instead of the host relaying pushes

Direct-mode sandboxes mount the host repo, so commits already land on the
host with no push needed — that part of the flow was already correct. This
kit is for closing the gap where a sandbox session wants to also push and
open the PR itself, without a human relaying `git push` / `gh pr create`
from the host each time.

input.old_string:
# entire kit

Installs `entire` and `git-remote-entire` in the sandbox so a session can
push through the `entire://` mirror itself, instead of handing push/PR
commands back to the host.
Also installs the `graph` plugin (`entire-graph`) as the agent user, so
`.entire/graph-agent.md`'s `entire graph search` workflow works inside the
sandbox — without it, a sandbox session has no plugin at
`~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin` and silently falls back to grep/find.

## One-time host setup

The binaries alone can't authenticate. Wire a token as a custom secret once,
on the host:

```bash
sbx secret set-custom \
  --host aws-eu-central-1.entire.io \
  --host us.auth.entire.io \
  --env ENTIRE_TOKEN \
  --command "entire auth token" \
  --refresh 55m
```

This stores the *command*, not a static token — `sbx` re-runs `entire auth
token` on the host and refreshes the sandbox's placeholder value every 55
minutes (the same cadence `entire auth token` itself uses to refresh a
near-expiry login JWT). The sandbox only ever sees a placeholder in
`ENTIRE_TOKEN`; the proxy substitutes the real bearer token on outbound
requests to the two hosts above.

If push still fails from other `*.entire.io` subdomains (a different
jurisdiction cell, for example), add more `--host` entries to the same
secret with `sbx secret set-custom ... --host <new-host>` — `set-custom`
overwrites in place when given the same `--env`/scope.

## Usage
input.new_string:
# entire kit

Installs `entire` and `git-remote-entire` in the sandbox for local CLI and
checkpoint use, plus the `graph` plugin (`entire-graph`) as the agent user,
so `.entire/graph-agent.md`'s `entire graph search` workflow works inside
the sandbox — without it, a sandbox session has no plugin at
`~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin` and silently falls back to grep/find.

This kit deliberately does **not** enable the sandbox to push or fetch
against `origin` (the `entire://` mirror) itself. It used to, via a
`ENTIRE_TOKEN` custom secret (`sbx secret set-custom`) — dropped because it
can't work: `git-remote-entire` parses `ENTIRE_TOKEN`'s JWT claims (`aud`,
to pick the core URL) **locally, before any network call**
(`cmd/entire/cli/auth/env_token.go` in `entireio/cli`), but `sbx secret
set-custom` only substitutes the real bearer token *on the wire*, for
requests to the declared hosts. The sandbox process itself only ever sees
the opaque placeholder (`sbx-cs-...`), so local claim-parsing always fails
with `parse ENTIRE_TOKEN claims: malformed JWT: expected 3 segments, got 1`
— this is a structural mismatch between the two mechanisms, not a
misconfiguration. `aws-eu-central-1.entire.io` / `us.auth.entire.io` were
removed from `permissions.network.allow` since nothing in this kit talks to
them anymore.

Direct-mode sandboxes mount the host repo, so commits already land on the
host with no push needed. Fetching a fresh `origin/main` (e.g. for
`git worktree add -b <branch> ../devdesk-<branch> origin/main`) and pushing
a branch / opening the PR are handled from the host instead.

The alternative — passing the real JWT directly via
`--env ENTIRE_TOKEN=$(entire auth token)` — was considered and rejected for
now: it works, but puts a real (if short-lived) bearer token in the
sandbox's plaintext environment instead of never leaving the proxy. Revisit
if the host-relay round-trip becomes the bottleneck.

## Usage

```powershell
sbx run --kit "$env:SBX_KITS\entire" claude .
```

`--kit` only applies at sandbox **creation** (like `--publish`); re-attaching
to an existing sandbox ignores it. Adding it to an already-created sandbox
needs `sbx rm` + `sbx create --kit` — `sbx kit add` refuses kits that
declare `setup.startup`, but this one only declares `setup.install`, so
`sbx kit add` should work here too if you want to retrofit a running
sandbox.

Direct-mode sandboxes mount the host repo, so commits already land on the
host with no push needed — that part of the flow was already correct. This
kit is for closing the gap where a sandbox session wants to also push and
open the PR itself, without a human relaying `git push` / `gh pr create`
from the host each time.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# entire kit

Installs `entire` and `git-remote-entire` in the sandbox for local CLI and
checkpoint use, plus the `graph` plugin (`entire-graph`) as the agent user,
so `.entire/graph-agent.md`'s `entire graph search` workflow works inside
the sandbox — without it, a sandbox session has no plugin at
`~/.local/share/entire/plugins/bin` and silently falls back to grep/find.

This kit deliberately does **not** enable the sandbox to push or fetch
against `origin` (the `entire://` mirror) itself. It used to, via a
`ENTIRE_TOKEN` custom secret (`sbx secret set-custom`) — dropped because it
can't work: `git-remote-entire` parses `ENTIRE_TOKEN`'s JWT claims (`aud`,
to pick the core URL) **locally, before any network call**
(`cmd/entire/cli/auth/env_token.go` in `entireio/cli`), but `sbx secret
set-custom` only substitutes the real bearer token *on the wire*, for
requests to the declared hosts. The sandbox process itself only ever sees
the opaque placeholder (`sbx-cs-...`), so local claim-parsing always fails
with `parse ENTIRE_TOKEN claims: malformed JWT: expected 3 segments, got 1`
— this is a structural mismatch between the two mechanisms, not a
misconfiguration. `aws-eu-central-1.entire.io` / `us.auth.entire.io` were
removed from `permissions.network.allow` since nothing in this kit talks to
them anymore.

Direct-mode sandboxes mount the host repo, so commits already land on the
host with no push needed. Fetching a fresh `origin/main` (e.g. for
`git worktree add -b <branch> ../devdesk-<branch> origin/main`) and pushing
a branch / opening the PR are handled from the host instead.

The alternative — passing the real JWT directly via
`--env ENTIRE_TOKEN=$(entire auth token)` — was considered and rejected for
now: it works, but puts a real (if short-lived) bearer token in the
sandbox's plaintext environment instead of never leaving the proxy. Revisit
if the host-relay round-trip becomes the bottleneck.

## Usage

```powershell
sbx run --kit "$env:SBX_KITS\entire" claude .
```

`--kit` only applies at sandbox **creation** (like `--publish`); re-attaching
to an existing sandbox ignores it. Adding it to an already-created sandbox
needs `sbx rm` + `sbx create --kit` — `sbx kit add` refuses kits that
declare `setup.startup`, but this one only declares `setup.install`, so
`sbx kit add` should work here too if you want to retrofit a running
sandbox.

content.content:
Manage stored secrets for sandbox environments.

SERVICE SECRETS (e.g. "github", "anthropic", "openai")
  When a sandbox starts, the proxy uses stored secrets to authenticate API
  requests on behalf of the agent. The secret is never exposed directly.
  Scoped globally (shared across all sandboxes) or to a specific sandbox.

REGISTRY SECRETS (e.g. "ghcr.io", "myregistry.azurecr.io")
  Used to pull private template images and kit artifacts before sandbox
  creation. Unlike service secrets, registry credentials are host-only by
  default. They are not injected into sandboxes unless --all-sandboxes or
  --sandbox is set (the credential never enters the sandbox filesystem).
  Use "sbx secret set --registry <host> --password-stdin" to store them.

Usage:
  sbx secret COMMAND

Available Commands:
  import      Import secrets detected in host environment variables
  ls          List stored secrets
  rm          Remove a secret
  set         Create or update a secret
  set-custom  (Experimental) Create or update a custom secret

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for secret

Global Flags:
  -D, --debug   Enable debug logging

Use "sbx secret COMMAND --help" for more information about a command.
---set---
Create or update a service secret or registry credential.

### Service secrets

Available services: anthropic, cursor, droid, github, google, groq, mistral, nebius, openai, openrouter, xai

Service secrets apply globally by default. Use --sandbox to scope a secret to
one sandbox. When SERVICE is omitted, an interactive prompt selects it.

### Dynamic secrets

Use --ref or --command to store a secret source instead of the secret value.
sbx resolves the source on the host when needed and caches the value according
to the --refresh policy.

--ref supports 1Password op:// references and AWS Secrets Manager ARNs. The
corresponding op or aws CLI must be installed and authenticated. --command
runs a shell command and uses its standard output as the secret value.

### Registry credentials

Use --registry to store pull credentials for a container registry. Unlike
service secrets, registry credentials are host-only by default:

- By default, credentials are used for template and kit pulls on the host.
  They are never injected into a sandbox.
- With --all-sandboxes, credentials are used for host pulls and injected by
  the proxy into every new sandbox's registry login. The credentials never
  enter the sandbox.
- With --sandbox, credentials are injected into the specified sandbox only.

Usage:
  sbx secret set [SERVICE] [flags]

Examples:
  # Store a GitHub token globally (available to all sandboxes)
  sbx secret set github

  # Store an OpenAI key for a specific sandbox
  sbx secret set openai --sandbox my-sandbox

  # Non-interactive via stdin (e.g., from a secret manager or env var)
  echo "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" | sbx secret set anthropic

  # Start OpenAI OAuth flow and store global OAuth tokens
  sbx secret set openai --oauth

  # Resolve a 1Password reference at use time (requires an authenticated op CLI)
  sbx secret set anthropic --ref 'op://Private/Anthropic/api-key'

  # Resolve an AWS Secrets Manager ARN at use time (requires an authenticated aws CLI)
  sbx secret set anthropic --ref 'arn:aws:secretsmanager:us-west-2:123456789012:secret:anthropic-api-key'

  # Resolve a secret using an arbitrary command
  sbx secret set github --command 'gh auth token'

  # Registry: host-only (template/kit pulls, not injected into sandboxes)
  gh auth token | sbx secret set --registry ghcr.io --password-stdin

  # Registry: host pulls + injected into every new sandbox
  gh auth token | sbx secret set --all-sandboxes --registry ghcr.io --password-stdin

  # Registry: specific sandbox only
  gh auth token | sbx secret set --sandbox my-sandbox --registry ghcr.io --password-stdin

Flags:
      --all-sandboxes     Inject registry credentials into every sandbox (requires --registry)
      --command string    Use a command's standard output as the secret value
  -f, --force             Overwrite an existing secret when --token is used
  -h, --help              help for set
      --no-verify         Skip checking the --ref or --command source when storing it
      --oauth             Start OAuth flow and store OAuth tokens (openai/global only)
      --password-stdin    Read registry password or token from stdin (use with --registry)
      --ref string        Use a 1Password op:// reference or AWS Secrets Manager ARN as the secret source
      --refresh string    Secret refresh policy: on-demand or after a duration (default: 55m)
      --registry string   Registry hostname for pull credentials (e.g. ghcr.io)
      --sandbox string    Scope the secret to one sandbox instead of its default scope
      --show-error        Show resolver standard error if the initial check fails (may contain secrets)
  -t, --token string      Secret value (less secure: visible in shell history)
      --username string   Registry username (use with --registry; omit for token-only auth)

Global Flags:
  -D, --debug   Enable debug logging

content.text:
Two things stacked up:

**Why it's asking for a token:** `sbx secret list` still shows a **global** custom secret from before we touched the kit — `ENTIRE_TOKEN → sbx-cs-1gL3tTlIaxgTqIUf, targets: aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/us.auth.entire.io`. Editing the kit's `spec.yaml`/README didn't remove this — it's separate host state, set once via `sbx secret set-custom`, and it applies to *every* sandbox regardless of kit. So the sandbox still gets the broken opaque placeholder injected, `git-remote-entire` still can't parse it as a JWT, same failure as before.

The fix the sandbox agent suggested — `sbx secret set entire --sandbox ... -t "<your entire token>"` — **doesn't exist**. `sbx secret set --help` lists the only valid services: `anthropic, cursor, droid, github, google, groq, mistral, nebius, openai, openrouter, xai`. `entire` isn't one of them; the agent invented that command.

**Good news — the commit isn't actually stuck.** `sbx ls` shows this sandbox mounts the `devdesk` directory itself (direct-mode), not a private clone. When the sandbox ran `git worktree add ../devdesk-feat-ge-create-row-spinner`, that sibling path fell *outside* the single mounted directory, so it landed in the sandbox's own private container layer — invisible from the host, which is why `git worktree list` showed it `prunable` (I've since pruned that stale entry). But the commit itself was written into `.git/objects`, which *is* shared — I found it already sitting in this host repo: `b698377 feat: créer et supprimer sont du travail, pas une attente (§3.59)`, on top of current `origin/main`.

And separately, want me to `sbx secret rm --placeholder sbx-cs-1gL3tTlIaxgTqIUf -f` to remove the stale global `ENTIRE_TOKEN` secret so this stops coming up in future sandboxes?

    Le dashboard, `ws` et `:sec` lisent le même workspace-scans.json, et deux
    d'entre eux écartaient ce que le troisième additionnait : un dépôt supprimé
    après son scan garde son entrée pour toujours — rien ne la retire, et un
    `rm -rf` fait hors de l'application n'est observé par personne.
    
    `:sec` réconciliait déjà à la lecture (`isGone`) et `ws` ne liste que le
    disque. `readPosture`, cinquième lecteur des deux mêmes caches, sommait tout :
    ses CRITICAL n'étaient donc visibles que sur le seul écran d'où l'on ne peut
    pas aller les voir. Un compteur qu'aucune vue ne sait détailler n'est pas un
    compteur.
    
    Le prédicat déménage en `internal/cache` (`RepositoryGone`), auprès des entrées
    qu'il juge, et les deux lecteurs l'appellent. `os.IsNotExist` et rien d'autre :
    un partage lent n'est pas une suppression.
    
    Effet de bord dans le bon sens — un dépôt supprimé compensait exactement un
    dépôt jamais scanné dans `uncovered()`, donc la boîte annonçait `0 unscanned`
    d'un ensemble où il en restait.
    
    La moitié « images » garde le même défaut, sciemment : le savoir demande
    d'énumérer le démon, et readPosture ne lit que deux fichiers.

commit 041e6395cb64b8129cc4a4d516b1224ec0934c13
Author: anthnel <anthnel@proton.me>
Date:   Sun Aug 30 16:04:56 2026 +0200

    fix: la posture écarte aussi les images disparues (D69, suite)
    
    Un `docker rmi` après un scan laissait ses CRITICAL dans l'arbre Images du
    dashboard, exactement comme une suppression de dépôt les laissait dans l'arbre
    Repositories. `:sec` les écartait déjà des deux côtés.
    
    Ce qui restait à trancher était l'appel au démon : readPosture ne lisait que des
    fichiers. L'asymétrie retenue est celle de Rule 110 — l'énumération est faite
    par le Cmd et passée en paramètre, `os.Stat` reste dedans. Lire un chemin est de
    la même nature que lire les deux fichiers de cache ; interroger un service qui
    peut être arrêté ne l'est pas. Un `docker image ls` par tour lent, sur l'horloge
    qui fait déjà un `docker system df`, et readPosture reste testable sans toucher
    à la couture.
    
    En le faisant, un troisième lecteur est apparu : internal/mcp (scan_inventory)
    tenait sa propre copie de toute la règle — la couture listImages, localImages,
    isGone. Elle était donc écrite deux fois, et absente là où elle manquait. Ce
    n'est pas une coïncidence : une règle recopiée est une règle que le lecteur
    suivant ne trouve pas.
    
    Chacune a une maison : cache.RepositoryGone et cache.ImageGone restent pures,
    docker.ImageNames porte l'appel au démon et le (nil, false) qui garde tout.
    C'est aussi la couture de test que les trois paquets déclaraient chacun pour
    soi ; mcp garde la sienne pour images_list, qui projette l'Image entière.
    
    Le garde compte double sur le dashboard : un démon éteint garde toutes les
    entrées, sans quoi la boîte Images afficherait `0 CRITICAL` — la seule mauvaise
    réponse que personne n'irait vérifier.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text:
No — cancel that `entire login` (Ctrl+C or close the browser tab), it's not the right move. Two things:

**Why it broke:** this is the direct fetch-side consequence of dropping `ENTIRE_TOKEN` — a freshly recreated sandbox now has *zero* entire auth, so **any** `origin` operation fails, not just push. `git pull` needs auth just as much as `git push` did.

**Why you shouldn't authenticate inside the sandbox anyway:** an interactive `entire login` there would store a real, persistent OAuth session (your actual `@anthnel` identity) inside the sandbox's filesystem — that's arguably a *bigger* standing credential exposure than the broken `ENTIRE_TOKEN` placeholder we removed, and it'd need re-doing on every sandbox recreation since nothing persists it. It reopens exactly the tradeoff we deliberately avoided last time.

**What to do instead:** this is a direct-mode sandbox — it mounts the same `devdesk` directory as the host, so it shares the *same* `.git`, including refs. It doesn't need to fetch anything itself: `origin/main` is already sitting there at `0f334d6` from my last merge on the host. So `git pull` is simply the wrong command to run in the sandbox — there's nothing to pull that isn't already local. Have it work directly off `origin/main`/`main` as-is (`git worktree add -b <branch> ../devdesk-<branch> origin/main`, no `git fetch` first), edit and commit locally, and when it's done, tell me and I'll fetch/push/PR/merge from here like the last three — same flow we've been running.

content.text:
Deux briques manquent, et pas la même pour chacune.

**1. `gh pr create`/`gh pr merge` (API GitHub, pas le mirror)** — rien de configuré (`sbx secret ls` ne montre que `anthropic`). C'est simple à fixer : `github` est un vrai *service secret* pris en charge nativement par sbx (comme `anthropic`), pas le bricolage custom qu'on a retiré. Un token GitHub est opaque — `gh` ne le décode pas côté client — donc ça n'a pas le problème de parsing JWT qu'on a eu avec `ENTIRE_TOKEN` :
```bash
sbx secret set github --command "gh auth token"
```

**2. `git push`/`git pull` vers `origin` (le mirror `entire://`)** — c'est le point qu'on a coupé. `CLAUDE.md` interdit formellement un second remote GitHub pour contourner ça (« *origin est le seul remote, délibérément* »), donc quelle que soit l'option, le push doit repasser par `git-remote-entire`, qui a besoin d'un vrai contexte d'auth. Deux façons de le lui donner, mêmes compromis qu'avant :

- **`entire login` interactif dans la sandbox** (ce que l'agent avait lancé) — fonctionne, stocke un vrai contexte de session dans le système de fichiers de la sandbox, mais à refaire à chaque recréation, et laisse un identifiant complet et persistant dans un environnement moins fiable que le host.
- **Réinjecter le vrai token au lancement** — `sbx run --kit ... --env ENTIRE_TOKEN=$(entire auth token) claude .` — pas de login interactif à refaire, mais un token réel (même court) en clair dans l'env de la sandbox. C'est exactement le compromis qu'on avait écarté en supprimant `ENTIRE_TOKEN` du kit.

Laquelle tu veux pour l'auth `entire` ?

## Docker Sandboxes Secret Management

Docker Sandboxes creates isolated sandbox environments for AI agents, powered by Docker.

### Service Secrets

Service secrets apply globally by default. Use --sandbox to scope a secret to one sandbox. The secrets manager works through a proxy mechanism: Docker Sandboxes run a credential proxy. In plain terms: The real secret stays on your host machine. The sandbox never gets the real token. It gets a fake stand-in called a sentinel.

### Secret Storage and Retrieval

sbx has a built-in secrets manager that stores credentials in your OS keychain — never in plain text on disk or inside the VM. Use --ref or --command to store a secret source instead of the secret value. sbx resolves the source on the host when needed and caches the value according to the --refresh policy.

Docker Sandboxes is a microVM-based runtime for running AI coding agents safely, wrapping each agent inside a lightweight virtual machine with its own Linux kernel.

## Secret Management

Docker Sandboxes keeps long-lived secrets on the host and injects them into outbound requests via the proxy, so real secrets never enter the sandbox. Secrets can be set via `sbx secret set` or pulled from files.

Docker Sandboxes keeps long-lived secrets on the host and injects them into outbound requests via the proxy, so real secrets never enter the sandbox. This works well for **static** credentials (API keys, PATs). It breaks for **OAuth access tokens**, which are short-lived (~1h) and must be refreshed from a refresh token + client secret.

Today, the only way to satisfy a `serviceAuth` header injection with an OAuth-protected API is to inject a **static** token (expires in ~1h) or to place the **refresh token + client secret inside the sandbox** and let the in-sandbox tool refresh. The latter defeats the entire point of the proxy model: a single sandbox compromise yields a long-lived credential to the underlying data - usable off-box and after the sandbox is gone.

**Ask:** allow a `serviceAuth` value to be sourced from a **host-side executable** that returns a **short-lived token plus its expiry**, which the proxy caches and refreshes. This keeps the long-lived material on the host, gives the sandbox only an ephemeral, host-confined bearer, and is a generalization of a pattern Sandboxes already provide.

## Motivating example: `gogcli` (Google Workspace) in a sandbox

We want an agent in a sandbox to read Google Calendar/Docs/Drive via [`gogcli`](https://github.com/openclaw/gogcli) (`gog`), authorized with a **read-only, Calendar/Docs-only** OAuth token from our own Google Cloud project.

Kit shape (not tested yet):

```yaml
network:
  serviceDomains:
    www.googleapis.com: googleapis
  serviceAuth:
    googleapis:
      headerName: Authorization
      valueFormat: "Bearer %s"
  allowedDomains:
    - oauth2.googleapis.com
    - docs.googleapis.com
```

The `%s` can be a static secret set via `sbx secret set` or pulled from an env var or a file. An access token expires in ~1h; a refresh token is exactly the long-lived secret we do not want in the sandbox.

## Proposed solution

Let a `credentials` source its value from a host-side credential provider instead of a static secret:

```yaml
network:
  serviceDomains:
    www.googleapis.com: googleapis
  serviceAuth:
    googleapis:
      headerName: Authorization
      valueFormat: "Bearer %s"
  allowedDomains:
    - oauth2.googleapis.com
    - docs.googleapis.com

Recherché sur `docker/sbx-releases` (le repo d'issues officiel de sbx) et via docs.docker.com — rien sur `entire`/`entireio` nulle part, aucune issue ouverte ne le demande.

L'issue la plus proche est **[#300 « Host-side credential providers for other OAuth services »](https://github.com/docker/sbx-releases/issues/300)** — une demande pour généraliser l'injection de token à l'échelle du proxy réseau (comme `sbx secret set-custom` aujourd'hui, mais avec refresh automatique pour des tokens OAuth courts). Problème : même si ça sortait, ça ne réglerait **pas** notre cas — le principe reste l'injection côté proxy réseau uniquement, jamais dans l'env de la sandbox elle-même. Or c'est exactement ce qui casse avec `entire` : `git-remote-entire` doit lire le vrai JWT **localement, avant tout appel réseau**, pas seulement l'envoyer sur le fil. Un token matérialisé dans l'env, aucune des solutions sbx actuelles ou en discussion ne le fait pour un secret custom — seul le mode `passthrough: true` le fait, et seulement pour les services intégrés en dur (`anthropic`, `github`, etc.), pas pour un service arbitraire comme `entire`.

Bref : rien à attendre côté sbx à court terme. Les trois options restent les mêmes qu'avant — tu veux qu'on reste sur le host-relay actuel, ou on met en place une des deux autres (login interactif / token réinjecté) ?

tree nobody is looking at. Siblings of the checkout (`../devdesk-<branch>`) keep
the module root holding one copy of the code, which is why they are not merely a
tidier choice.

**What isolates, and what does not.** git refuses to check out one branch in two
worktrees, so two agents cannot land on the same branch by accident — that is the
whole protection, and it is worth knowing what it does *not* cover:

| Shared by every worktree | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `~/.devdesk/` — contexts, `config.yaml`, scan caches | two agents editing settings or scanning at once overwrite each other's; nothing warns |
| the host keyring, Docker, the ports the app binds | one at a time, whoever gets there first |
| `.git/hooks` | verified: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` resolves to the **main** checkout's, so the Entire checkpoint and pre-push hooks fire normally from a worktree |
| `origin` | inherited — `git push -u origin <branch>` goes through the mirror as usual |

`mise` tasks and `go build` work unchanged; both read the tree they are run in.

**`entire graph` indexes per directory.** A fresh worktree has no index, so the
first `entire graph search` there pays a full build (~5 s on this repo, measured)
and the symbol ids it returns are namespaced by the directory name
(`local/devdesk-<branch>:Go:…`). Nothing breaks; do not be surprised by the
first search being slow or by ids that do not match another worktree's.

**Clean up when the PR is merged**, from the main checkout:

```bash
git worktree remove ../devdesk-<branch>
git worktree list          # what is still out there
git worktree prune         # after a directory was deleted by hand
```

`git worktree remove` refuses a tree with uncommitted changes, which is the
point — look before forcing.

**The main checkout stays on `main` and stays clean.** It is what `git fetch
origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` needs after each merge, and what
every new worktree is cut from.

## Git workflow — pull requests only

**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:

```
! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
```

123	
124	This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub, and **Entire does not document it**
125	— neither the CLI help nor `docs.entire.io` mentions a protected default branch.
126	The only branch restriction Entire states is that `entire/unmirrored/*` is never
127	forwarded. Treat the rejection as observed behaviour, not as a specified one.
128	
129	What rules GitHub out is that branch protection is *unavailable* on this
130	repository: it is private on a free personal plan, so both endpoints answer
131	`403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public` —
132	`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main/protection` and `/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets`
133	alike. Do not cite `gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main` reporting
134	`"protected": false` as the proof: that field only ever reflects legacy branch
135	protection, so it reads `false` under a ruleset too, and on this plan it would
136	read `false` whatever the configuration. The 403 is the evidence; the `false` is
137	not.
138	
139	Every other branch, including `entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror
140	and is forwarded to GitHub.
141

### Landing a sandbox-made commit (host-relay)

A Docker Sandbox (`sbx`) has no `entire://` auth of its own — `ENTIRE_TOKEN`
via `sbx secret set-custom` doesn't work (`git-remote-entire` parses the
JWT's claims locally, before any network call, but the secret proxy only
substitutes the real token on the wire — the sandbox process itself only
ever sees an unparseable placeholder), and an interactive `entire login`
inside the sandbox trades that for a persistent, harder-to-reason-about
credential sitting in a less-trusted place. So the sandbox edits and commits
locally only; the host does every `origin` operation — fetch, push, PR,
merge. `git pull`/`git fetch` run *inside* the sandbox will fail with `no
auth context for cluster ...` — that's expected, not a setup bug; don't
`entire login` there to fix it (see `~/projects/github/anthnel/sbx-kits/entire/README.md`
for the full rationale).

A direct-mode sandbox mounts this exact repo directory, so its commits land
straight in the shared `.git` — the host sees them immediately, no transfer
needed. But `git worktree add -b <branch> ../devdesk-<branch> ...` run
*inside* the sandbox creates that sibling path **outside** the single
mounted directory, so it lands in the sandbox's own private container
layer — invisible to the host (`git worktree list` shows it `prunable`).
The commit object itself is still in the shared `.git/objects` though, so
nothing is actually lost:

```bash
# From the host, once the sandbox reports "done and committed":
git worktree list                      # confirm the sibling worktree, prunable, HEAD sha
git cat-file -t <sha>                  # confirm the commit is really in this .git (it is)
git worktree prune -v                  # drop the stale, unreachable admin entry

git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/<branch>
gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch> \
  --title "<subject line>" --body "$(git show -s --format=%b <sha>)"
gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see above
```

**A follow-up commit on the same branch, after the first one already got
squash-merged, will conflict on a plain `git merge`** — squashing rewrites
history, so `git merge origin/main` computes the wrong common ancestor
(the branch's *own* pre-squash parent) and re-diffs files that already
landed, even when nothing actually conflicts in substance. Don't hand-edit
through that; cherry-pick the new commit straight onto current `origin/main`
instead — its real parent already matches what's on `main`, so it applies
clean:

```bash
git worktree add -b <tmp-branch> ../devdesk-<tmp-branch> <new-sha>
cd ../devdesk-<tmp-branch>
git reset --hard origin/main
git cherry-pick <new-sha>              # clean apply — verify before trusting this
go build ./... && go test ./<touched-packages>/...
git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch-name>
# gh pr create / gh pr merge as above, then from the main checkout:
git worktree remove ../devdesk-<tmp-branch>
```

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	> [!IMPORTANT]
6	> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
7	> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
8	>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
9	> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
10	>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
11	>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`.
12	> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
13	>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
14	>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.
15	
16	## Project Overview
17	
18	DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
19	- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
20	- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
21	- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
22	- Docker container management with real-time metrics
23	- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
24	- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces
25	- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
26	- Local workspaces management with git metadata
27	
28	## Build and Development Commands
29	
30	Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.
31	
32	```bash
33	# Development (fastest)
34	mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
35	go run .
36	
37	# Build
38	mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
39	mise run run          # Build and run
40	
41	# Testing
42	mise run test         # Run all tests
43	mise run cover        # Coverage per package
44	go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
45	go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
46	mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)
47	
48	# Code Quality
49	mise run fmt          # Format code
50	mise run vet          # Run go vet
51	mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
52	mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
53	mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
54	
55	# Installation
56	mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
57	```
58	
59	`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.
60	
61	## Work starts in a new worktree
62	
63	**Any task that will produce a commit begins with its own worktree**, cut from
64	the current `main`, outside the repository directory:
65	
66	```bash
67	git fetch origin main
68	git worktree add -b <branch> ../devdesk-<branch> origin/main
69	cd ../devdesk-<branch>
70	```
71	
72	Answering a question, reading code, running the app — none of that needs one.
73	Editing does.
74	
75	**Outside the repository, not under it.** A worktree placed at `.worktrees/x`
76	would be a second copy of every package inside the module root: `go build ./...`
77	and `go test ./...` would walk into it, compile it, and report failures from a
78	tree nobody is looking at. Siblings of the checkout (`../devdesk-<branch>`) keep
79	the module root holding one copy of the code, which is why they are not merely a
80	tidier choice.
81	
82	**What isolates, and what does not.** git refuses to check out one branch in two
83	worktrees, so two agents cannot land on the same branch by accident — that is the
84	whole protection, and it is worth knowing what it does *not* cover:
85	
86	| Shared by every worktree | Consequence |
87	|---|---|

119

122	```

125	— neither the CLI help nor `docs.entire.io` mentions a protected default branch.
126	The only branch restriction Entire states is that `entire/unmirrored/*` is never
127	forwarded. Treat the rejection as observed behaviour, not as a specified one.

130	repository: it is private on a free personal plan, so both endpoints answer
131	`403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public` —
132	`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main/protection` and `/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets`
133	alike. Do not cite `gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main` reporting
134	`"protected": false` as the proof: that field only ever reflects legacy branch
135	protection, so it reads `false` under a ruleset too, and on this plan it would
136	read `false` whatever the configuration. The 403 is the evidence; the `false` is
137	not.

139	Every other branch, including `entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror
140	and is forwarded to GitHub.

143	concept — it layers checkpoints and sessions over git and forwards pushes. So

159	remote pointing at a GitHub host, and `origin` is an `entire://` URL, so it
160	finds none and fails with *"none of the git remotes configured for this

180	`docs/backlog.md`.** Every fix inserts its entry at the top of §1.1, so the

184	### Landing a sandbox-made commit (host-relay)
185	
186	A Docker Sandbox (`sbx`) has no `entire://` auth of its own — `ENTIRE_TOKEN`
187	via `sbx secret set-custom` doesn't work (`git-remote-entire` parses the
188	JWT's claims locally, before any network call, but the secret proxy only
189	substitutes the real token on the wire — the sandbox process itself only
190	ever sees an unparseable placeholder), and an interactive `entire login`
191	inside the sandbox trades that for a persistent, harder-to-reason-about
192	credential sitting in a less-trusted place. So the sandbox edits and commits
193	locally only; the host does every `origin` operation — fetch, push, PR,
194	merge. `git pull`/`git fetch` run *inside* the sandbox will fail with `no
195	auth context for cluster ...` — that's expected, not a setup bug; don't
196	`entire login` there to fix it (see `~/projects/github/anthnel/sbx-kits/entire/README.md`
197	for the full rationale).
198	
199	A direct-mode sandbox mounts this exact repo directory, so its commits land
200	straight in the shared `.git` — the host sees them immediately, no transfer
201	needed. But `git worktree add -b <branch> ../devdesk-<branch> ...` run
202	*inside* the sandbox creates that sibling path **outside** the single
203	mounted directory, so it lands in the sandbox's own private container
204	layer — invisible to the host (`git worktree list` shows it `prunable`).
205	The commit object itself is still in the shared `.git/objects` though, so
206	nothing is actually lost:
207	
208	```bash
209	# From the host, once the sandbox reports "done and committed":
210	git worktree list                      # confirm the sibling worktree, prunable, HEAD sha
211	git cat-file -t <sha>                  # confirm the commit is really in this .git (it is)
212	git worktree prune -v                  # drop the stale, unreachable admin entry
213	
214	git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/<branch>
215	gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch> \
216	  --title "<subject line>" --body "$(git show -s --format=%b <sha>)"
217	gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch

219	```

222	squash-merged, will conflict on a plain `git merge`** — squashing rewrites
223	history, so `git merge origin/main` computes the wrong common ancestor
224	(the branch's *own* pre-squash parent) and re-diffs files that already
225	landed, even when nothing actually conflicts in substance. Don't hand-edit
226	through that; cherry-pick the new commit straight onto current `origin/main`
227	instead — its real parent already matches what's on `main`, so it applies
228	clean:
229	
230	```bash
231	git worktree add -b <tmp-branch> ../devdesk-<tmp-branch> <new-sha>
232	cd ../devdesk-<tmp-branch>
233	git reset --hard origin/main
234	git cherry-pick <new-sha>              # clean apply — verify before trusting this

236	git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch-name>

238	git worktree remove ../devdesk-<tmp-branch>
239	```

241	### Remotes
242	
243	| Remote | URL | Use |
244	|--------|-----|-----|
245	| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — everything: clone, fetch, push |
246

250	regional path, it is what keeps agent reads fast, and it is where the checkpoint

255	**not available in the EU region** — the server answers `semantic search is not

259	## Architecture
260	
261	The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
262	**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is

267	|---|---|
268	| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one spinner chain and the `:jobs` view |
